PullRequest.Title: agentHost: preserve MCP App tool-result _meta for restored cards
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #343243

Agent Host rebuilt MCP App `ui/notifications/tool-result` notifications from session state without the server's result `_meta`. App-only data (e.g. `_meta.flint.board` in the issue) was lost when a card was reconstructed, including after reopening a session or restarting.

### Changes
- The Copilot runtime now reports the verbatim MCP `CallToolResult._meta` on `tool.execution_complete` as `result.mcpResultMeta`, for MCP App tools only (github/copilot-agent-runtime#30458). It is separate from the IFC-only `mcpMeta`.
- Adds `resultMetadata?: Record<string, unknown>` to AHP `ToolCallResult`, mirroring MCP `CallToolResult._meta` the same way `structuredContent` mirrors `structuredContent`. The canonical protocol change is microsoft/agent-host-protocol#549; the synced types here are updated to match. The protocol reducer, result confirmation (`agentSideEffects`), and conversation import validation carry it like `structuredContent`.
- `copilotAgentSession.ts` (live completion) and `mapSessionEvents.ts` (history replay) set `resultMetadata` from the runtime's `mcpResultMeta`. Host-owned tool-call `_meta` (`ui`, `toolKind`, ...) is untouched.
- `stateToProgressAdapter.ts` (`toMcpCallToolResult`) rebuilds `resultMetadata` as the MCP result `_meta` for completed tools only. Metadata-only (`content: []`) and error results count as real results.
- Model-facing conversion (`agentHostMcpAppToolsService._convertResult`) is unchanged and does not include result `_meta`.
- The pinned `@github/copilot-sdk` does not declare `mcpResultMeta` yet, so `getSdkMcpResultMeta` reads it through a narrow cast (TODO to remove after the SDK bump). With an older runtime the field is absent and behavior is unchanged.

### How to test
1. Run a runtime/SDK build that includes github/copilot-agent-runtime#30458.
2. Add an MCP App server whose tool result carries `_meta`. The ext-apps `basic-server-vanillajs` example with a per-call `_meta.example.verificationToken` works; it displays the received token.
3. In an Agent Host chat, have the model call the tool. The card shows the token. Reopen the session and restart VS Code: the same token is shown. **Get Server Time** shows a new one.

### Validation
- `scripts/test.bat --run` on agentMetaReaders, agentHostCreateSessionImportMeta, copilotAgentSession, mapSessionEvents, reducers, agentSideEffects, stateToProgressAdapter, and agentHostMcpAppToolsService tests: 2334 passing.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passes against the pinned SDK, and against a local SDK that declares the field.
- `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean.
- Manual end to end with a local runtime build and the example above: live, reopened, and cold-restarted cards all received the original token.

<sub>Written by Connor's agent</sub>

Scenarios.Scenario: Live MCP App tool completion and card update
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The runtime emits one tool.execution_complete event; CopilotAgentSession emits one ChatToolCallComplete action, the reducer commits it, the subscribed workbench receives it, and an initialized MCP App card receives one ui/notifications/tool-result notification. These steps are on the result/card update path; no new await or synchronous collection-wide work was added.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Carry the already-received runtime mcpResultMeta in the existing ChatToolCallComplete action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing runtime completion/action per completed MCP App invocation; effective cardinality is one metadata object per result, with no per-property boundary calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same completion event and action were emitted without resultMetadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The completion action must reach state/UI before the completed card is available; the diff increases payload bytes but adds no boundary round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing action notification to each relevant subscribed client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One send per relevant connected client for the completion action; metadata does not change client fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The completion action was already broadcast to the same subscribers without this field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing state synchronization boundary; only the serialized action size grows by the metadata size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post the reconstructed CallToolResult to the MCP App webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing tool-result notification per initialized completed card (or once when a live invocation completes).
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same notification carried content, structuredContent, and error state but omitted result _meta.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the app to consume its result; the diff adds _meta to the existing notification rather than adding another notification.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of completed MCP App calls, number of relevant connected clients, and total JSON size of each result _meta. The reducer and adapter retain/reuse object references and do not traverse or deep-copy nested metadata.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Completion remains event-driven with one action per tool invocation. Protocol broadcast fans out to currently subscribed clients and the webview notification is sent once when the card initializes or completes; the diff adds no loop over tools and no new limiter or burst behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is introduced. Completed tool state retains one metadata reference for the loaded conversation, and the MCP App model reuses the reconstructed result; empty and missing metadata remain distinguishable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the complete event-to-action-to-adapter-to-webview path is explicit, and each changed line adds a field without changing call count or scheduling.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: MCP result metadata is open-ended, so exact payload sizes vary by server, but the changed cost is linear payload retention/serialization on boundaries already required by the result.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The intentional payload preservation adds linear bytes but no repeated reconstruction, extra boundary operation, unbounded cache, or concurrency amplification.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold session restore, history replay, and reopening an MCP App card
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold restore, persisted SDK events are read, mapSessionEvents builds completed tool-call states including resultMetadata, turns are synchronized to the client, and the adapter constructs the card result. Warm reads use the existing mapped-event promise/state; rendering the card then sends its existing tool-result notification.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read persisted runtime events in pages of up to 1000 events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing paginated history reads based on event count; the diff does not increase request count, though returned event bytes include metadata supplied by the runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same persisted events were read and mapped, but the mapped tool-call state dropped mcpResultMeta.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold restore waits for the existing history read and mapping; warm memoized reads do not repeat it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the existing session database and restore stored shell/resource outputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing database scope per history reconstruction plus existing resource restoration work; result metadata causes no database operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical database access occurred while metadata was omitted from mapped tool-call state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing restore boundary remains on the cold path and is unaffected in count or placement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize loaded turns, including completed tool-call metadata, to the client.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing turns-loaded action per loaded history page/window, carrying all turns in that page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The action already transported the same turns without resultMetadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: History display waits for this existing action; payload bytes increase linearly with metadata in loaded MCP App results.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Persisted event/turn count in the loaded history window and aggregate result-metadata bytes across completed MCP App calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Persisted event pages are fetched by the existing reader and mapped once per memoized scope. Reads of events and session metadata may run in parallel as before; metadata adds no additional task or per-result I/O.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold restore reads and maps events. CopilotAgentSession memoizes mapped events by primary/all scope, and isolated history reads memoize by chat identity; rejected reads are evicted. Warm access reuses the promise/result and does not re-read metadata.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both history callers, their paging, memoization, mapping, and adapter conversion were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and size of app results varies, but loaded-history cardinality and page behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff preserves data in an already-loaded result and does not add reads, defeat memoization, or multiply mapping work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Conversation import or move to a remote agent host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The client serializes the imported conversation once. Payloads at or below 1 MiB use the existing createSession request; larger payloads are split into 1 MiB chunks and sent sequentially before createSession. Result metadata now contributes to the serialized transcript size.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify the full imported conversation, now including resultMetadata accepted by the import schema.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full serialization per imported conversation; work scales with total transcript bytes, including metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same transcript was serialized once, but completed tool results had no resultMetadata field to include.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization is on the session-create critical path as before; metadata adds only its own linear bytes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the direct createSession request or sequential staged import chunks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request below the 1 MiB threshold; otherwise ceil(serialized UTF-16 code units / 1 MiB) staged requests plus createSession. Metadata can increase bytes and may cross an existing chunk boundary, but does not create per-tool requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same threshold and sequential chunking applied to a transcript that omitted result metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Chunk transfer must finish before remote session creation, as before.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Aggregate imported transcript size, especially total MCP App result-metadata bytes across historical tool calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Large imports deliberately serialize extension requests one chunk at a time; the diff does not alter this sequencing or create parallel requests.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no import cache; each explicit import serializes once. Staged chunks are temporary transfer data, and bulky import metadata is removed after extraction by existing code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serializer, 1 MiB threshold, chunk splitter, and sequential request loop were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Open metadata can vary in size and may add chunks, but there is no evidence in the diff of duplicate encoding, pre-cap transformation, or realistic pathological amplification beyond the required bytes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Carrying required metadata increases transfer proportionally, while existing chunking bounds each request and no avoidable duplicate serialization or per-result boundary fan-out is introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 15 changed files. The change preserves one open metadata object per completed MCP App result through existing live, replay, confirmation, import, and webview paths. Costs scale linearly with required payload bytes; object references are reused, history reads remain memoized/paged, import remains chunked, and no new expensive-boundary call count, eager work, repeated work, cache leak, or concurrency burst was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
